title: Client-Side JWT Payload Decoding Without Cryptographic Signature Verification
description: Client-side decoding in jwt.ts extracts claims from unsigned JWT payloads to gate navigation in AdminRoute.
claimed_root_cause: The frontend decodes JWT claims using atob without verifying HMAC or RSA cryptographic signatures on the client.

trace.description: Splits JWT into segments and decodes payload without cryptographic verification.
Gates client-side UI route rendering using isJwtAdmin(token).

evidence.description: Architectural documentation explicitly specifies client decoding is for UI routing only; real access control is enforced by Spring Security @PreAuthorize.
AdminRoute documentation specifies that backend Spring Security remains authoritative for real authorization.

reason: Not a vulnerability. In single-page web architecture, client-side signature verification is technically infeasible without shipping the backend secret key or public key in client bundles. The backend authoritatively enforces @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") on all admin endpoints.

title: Client-Accessible Cookie Storage for Authentication Tokens
description: Access and refresh tokens are stored in document.cookie without HttpOnly flags because the current backend returns tokens in JSON response bodies.
claimed_root_cause: The frontend sets tokens into document.cookie with SameSite=Lax and Secure, but cannot set HttpOnly from client-side JavaScript.

trace.description: Writes token to document.cookie with path=/; SameSite=Lax.
Reads token from document.cookie for API requests.

evidence.description: Codebase comments record that backend should set HttpOnly cookies in Set-Cookie headers rather than JSON body.

blockers: Requires Spring Boot backend modification to issue Set-Cookie: refreshToken=...; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict headers on /api/v1/auth/login and /api/v1/auth/refresh.

validation_plan.local: Verify that document.cookie cannot set HttpOnly and requires backend Set-Cookie response header.
validation_plan.deployment: Inspect production Set-Cookie headers on https://api.connect2code.in/api/v1/auth/login to confirm if HttpOnly cookies are issued.

title: Potential Credential Exposure in Logout Exception Logging
description: The logout method logs the raw exception object to the browser console, potentially exposing the request configuration and token payload in console logs.
root_cause: console.warn in authService.ts logs the raw Axios error object which may include error.config.data containing the refresh token.
intended_behavior: Logout failure should log only a sanitized error string without dumping request payloads or headers.

trace.description: Passes refreshToken in payload to logout API endpoint.
Logs raw exception e to console.warn upon network failure.

evidence.description: console.warn('Logout API warning:', e) logs the entire error object.

conditions.description: User clicks logout when network fails or server responds with an error.

execution.attacker_perspective: A user or attacker with access to browser console or extension inspection could inspect logged Axios error objects to retrieve tokens.
instructions: Call authService.logout() when server is unreachable
execution.observed_result: Full error object including configuration data is output to console.

remediation.strategy: Log only the error message or an innocuous string, omitting the raw error object.

code_changes.fixed_code: console.warn('Logout API warning:', e instanceof Error ? e.message : 'Logout request unfulfilled');

likelihood.reason: Requires console access or extension log extraction on the client machine.

impact.reason: Refreshed tokens are already invalidated on server-side logout in normal operations.

confidence.reason: Directly visible in authService.ts:121 source code.

title: Client-Side Open Redirect in Login Redirection Flow
description: Login component redirects users to an unsanitized targetUrl taken from navigation state or sessionStorage without applying protocol or origin validation.
root_cause: Login.tsx navigates directly to targetUrl without validating that the target is a relative internal path, allowing external protocol or domain redirection.
intended_behavior: targetUrl must be validated and sanitized using getSafeRedirectUrl, restricting navigation to safe internal relative paths.

trace.description: Extracts from destination from navLocationState or sessionStorage post_auth_redirect.
Assigns targetUrl from untrusted from variable without URL sanitization.
Calls navigate(targetUrl, { replace: true }) where targetUrl could be external.

evidence.description: navigate(targetUrl, { replace: true }) called without getSafeRedirectUrl.
OAuthCallback implements getSafeRedirectUrl specifically to prevent open redirects, but the helper was not shared or used in Login.tsx.

conditions.description: Victim follows a crafted link to /login with state or manipulated redirect state and logs in.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker crafts a link or manipulates post_auth_redirect to an external phishing domain.
instructions: Observer that React Router navigates off-site
execution.observed_result: User is redirected to the external URL upon login completion.

remediation.strategy: Centralize getSafeRedirectUrl in a shared security utility and apply it to targetUrl in Login.tsx.

code_changes.fixed_code: const safeTarget = getSafeRedirectUrl(targetUrl); navigate(safeTarget, { replace: true });

likelihood.reason: Attacker can influence redirect state or from location property via crafted navigation.

impact.reason: Enables phishing attacks by redirecting authenticated users to an attacker-controlled site.

confidence.reason: Source code review directly proves lack of sanitization in Login.tsx.

title: Cross-Window Message Token Injection Risk & Broken Popup Flow
description: AppRouterLayout handleOAuthMessage requires event.data.token to trigger session refresh, exposing a Login CSRF risk if untrusted tokens are accepted and breaking the standard popup flow which does not transmit tokens.
root_cause: AppRouterLayout passes event.data token to refreshSessionThunk while OAuthCallback sends no token in postMessage.
intended_behavior: Popup message should strictly trigger cookie-based session synchronization without accepting arbitrary tokens from event.data.

trace.description: Listens for message events on window.
Calls dispatch(refreshSessionThunk(token)) with event.data token.

evidence.description: const token = event.data.refreshToken || event.data.token; if (token) { dispatch(refreshSessionThunk(token)); }
window.opener.postMessage({ type: 'C2C_GOOGLE_OAUTH_SUCCESS' }, window.location.origin) sends no token.

conditions.description: Popup OAuth window completes authentication and sends success notification.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker attempts to inject an arbitrary token into the parent window via postMessage.
instructions: Post message with type C2C_GOOGLE_OAUTH_SUCCESS and an attacker token
Parent window attempts to establish session with attacker token
execution.observed_result: Parent window executes refresh with untrusted token payload.

remediation.strategy: Invalidate in-memory session and invoke refreshSessionThunk without arguments so the authenticated cookie is used.

impact.reason: Prevents popup OAuth session completion and guards against token injection.

confidence.reason: Discrepancy verified between OAuthCallback postMessage payload and AppRouterLayout message listener.

title: Exposure of OAuth Credential Tokens in URL Parameters
description: OAuthCallback does not strip authentication tokens from window.location upon mount or failure, leaving sensitive tokens in browser history, address bar, and Referer headers.
root_cause: OAuthCallback does not sanitize window.location or history.replaceState to remove token parameters from query string.
intended_behavior: Sensitive OAuth parameters (token, refreshToken, accessToken) should be immediately extracted into memory and stripped from the browser URL.

trace.description: Navigates to /oauth/callback preserving full location.search and location.hash.
Mounts with sensitive query parameters retained in window.location.

evidence.description: On authentication error, component renders error view while tokens remain visible in browser address bar.

conditions.description: OAuth provider or backend redirects with token in query parameters.

execution.attacker_perspective: Attacker views browser history, shoulder-surfs, or reads Referer header if user clicks a link.
instructions: Check window.location.search after failure or delay
execution.observed_result: Tokens remain persistent in browser address bar and history.

remediation.strategy: Extract token parameters immediately into memory and replace browser history state with a sanitized URL.

likelihood.reason: Occurs whenever OAuth callback URL contains credentials in query string.

impact.reason: Token disclosure via browser history, shoulder surfing, and Referer headers.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspection of OAuthCallback.tsx and AppRouterLayout.tsx.

title: Direct Exposure of Judge0 API Keys or Endpoints to Frontend Clients
description: Hypothesis that Judge0 compiler credentials or endpoints are accessible to the frontend client.
claimed_root_cause: The frontend communicates directly with Judge0 API or bundles Judge0 keys.

trace.description: Calls API_ENDPOINTS.EXECUTION.USER_RUN via apiClient.
Resolves to Spring Boot backend /api/v1/runCode endpoint.

evidence.description: All execution calls target Spring Boot backend endpoints (/api/v1/runCode, /api/v1/submitCode); no direct Judge0 endpoint is ever called.

reason: Refuted by source code. The frontend communicates strictly with the Spring Boot backend proxy. Judge0 server details, tokens, and keys are never present in frontend source or bundles.

title: Cross-Site Scripting via Untrusted Compiler Output or Error Messages
description: Hypothesis that Judge0 execution output, actualOutput, or compiler error messages are rendered unsafely via innerHTML or unescaped HTML.
claimed_root_cause: Code execution results rendered into DOM without escaping.

trace.description: Receives actualOutput and errorMessage from backend.
Renders activeRunCase.actualOutput in JSX.

evidence.description: Output is rendered as JSX text node {activeRunCase.actualOutput}, which React automatically escapes.

reason: Refuted by source code. React JSX syntax automatically escapes string expressions as DOM text nodes. No dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML is used anywhere in problem execution components.

title: Client-Side User ID Manipulation for Profile and Registration Data Access
description: Hypothesis that frontend profile page allows viewing or modifying other users' profiles by manipulating route parameters.
claimed_root_cause: Frontend profile page accepts user-controlled ID parameter to fetch arbitrary user records.

trace.description: Profile route is mapped to static /profile without URL ID parameter.
Resolves effectiveUserId strictly from authenticated session state.

evidence.description: effectiveUserId is derived exclusively from authUser.id, profile.id, storedUser.id, or JWT claims.

reason: Refuted by source code. The profile route (/profile) does not accept a user ID parameter. User ID is determined exclusively from the authenticated session.

title: DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via dangerouslySetInnerHTML or eval
description: Hypothesis that untrusted user content is injected into the DOM using raw HTML escape hatches.
claimed_root_cause: Usage of dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, or eval on user-controlled inputs.

trace.description: Inspects entire frontend source tree for raw DOM injection APIs.
Evaluates presence of unsafe sinks.

evidence.description: All dynamic content rendered using standard React JSX curly brace expressions.

reason: Refuted by exhaustive codebase search. There are 0 occurrences of dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, outerHTML, document.write, eval(), or Function() anywhere in the src/ directory.
